title: Shipping Distance Calculator: Port to Port
description: Estimate port-to-port shipping distance with the Shipping Distance Calculator — sea distances in nautical miles, with honest notes on real routes. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, New York to London measures about 3,008 nautical miles port to port on the sphere — roughly 6.3 days of steaming at 20 knots before real sea routes add their detours.

Canals and straits decide the factor
popular_table.note: Published port-to-port sea distances come from routing tables that follow navigable water. This tool computes the geometric baseline those tables start from — never quote it as the sailed distance.

faq: Why is the real sailed distance longer?

Ships follow water: out of harbour channels, through straits and canals, around headlands and traffic separation schemes. Each constraint adds miles to the geometric baseline — 5–30% is typical, far more when a canal detour replaces a landmass crossing.
Major world ports by name, and any two points by coordinates — the geometry is the same once the endpoints are fixed. Harbour-to-harbour precision lives in professional routing tables.
Can it route via Suez or Panama?
No — this is a baseline calculator, not a routing engine. It tells you the distance the canal route will be compared against, which is the number that makes canal fees intelligible.
What speed should I assume for transit time?
Container services typically run 16–22 knots; bulk carriers slower, often 11–14. Take the carrier's service speed, divide distance by it, then add port and canal time generously.
Nautical or land miles for freight?
The sea trades in nautical miles and knots exclusively — quotes, charts and ETAs all assume them. This page reports both so land-side readers can translate.
Weather routing lengthens the sailed path to avoid storms — another reason the baseline is a floor. Seasonal planning uses weather-adjusted distances from routing services.
River reaches (the Mississippi, the Rhine) are channel distances, not great circles — the baseline understates them the most. Treat river legs with dedicated inland tables.
From published port-distance tables and routing software built on navigable-water graphs — then experience. This calculator's role is the independent check that keeps quotes honest.
